ops.title: DECIDED: the spawn gate stays /bin/sh — the Go re-exec rearchitecture is rejected, not deferred
ops.body:
Phase-1 lane P1-b was briefed to "replace the /bin/sh spawn gate with Go on both sides of the fork" (remediation plan, Phase 1 item 1). It returned a shape-change instead of implementing. The orchestrator decided **Option A: keep /bin/sh, delete only the TERM mask.** Recording the reasoning so nobody re-derives the rearchitecture and re-proposes it.

## What was measured (reproduced, not inferred)

A byte-identical copy of `proc/manager.go:24`'s `childWrapper`, with the same pipe/`ExtraFiles`/`Setsid` topology as `prepareCommand`, run standalone:

```
parked pid=66340 marker='r'
RESULT: parked wrapper SURVIVED SIGTERM (TERM-immune)
EOF path: exited after 625.584µs err=exit status 125
```

1. **TERM immunity at the gate is real** — the one live defect, exactly as briefed.
2. **The EOF path is already correct at HEAD**: 626µs, blocking read, no CPU spin. The busy-spin died with `2b912d6`. The briefed acceptance test "EOF exits 125 in bounded time and bounded CPU, proven red" **cannot be proven red** — it is a regression guard, not a defect fix.
3. **`childWrapper` is duplicated nowhere** — `proc/manager.go:23` (declaration) and `:1140` (use), that is all. The brief's "ONE shared implementation … no copies" clause had no target.

## Why "the gate in Go on both sides of the fork" is not reachable as briefed

Go exposes no post-fork/pre-exec hook — darwin's `syscall.SysProcAttr` carries only Chroot/Credential/Ptrace/Setsid/Setpgid/Setctty/Noctty/Ctty/Foreground/Pgid (verified against go1.26.5), and Go forbids running Go code between fork and exec in a multithreaded runtime. Separately, `Prepare` structurally *requires* a live parked pid: `proc/manager.go:399-428` forks the wrapper, `Probe`s its pid, `reaper.TrackGroup`s it durably, and only then awaits readiness — the durable record must exist before the target runs, so the gate cannot move into the parent. That leaves **re-exec of `os.Executable()`** as the only way to get Go on the child side.

## Why re-exec is rejected on the merits

- **It contradicts the remediation's own direction.** RC5 names "peer trust runs as a fork/exec of `os.Executable()`, putting a fork-bomb primitive and a load-dependent startup probe into every consumer" as a root cause to *remove*. Adding a second self-exec primitive to every consumer binary while deleting the first is incoherent.
- **It reintroduces RC3.** `deployment` atomically replaces the daemon binary, so a gate child spawned mid-upgrade execs the **new** binary — the gate protocol would have to be frozen forever, which is exactly the exact-match-across-a-flag-day shape this work exists to delete.
- **It disturbs the identity tuple.** The parked child's `Probe()` identity (`Comm`, `Executable`) changes from `sh`/`/bin/sh` to the daemon's own, touching the reaper comparison site the child-record-lifetime contract pins — the tuple that was widened five times, each widening missing one of ~8 open-coded comparisons in `proc/reaper.go`.
- **It taxes every spawn.** `worker.Pool` pays a full Go runtime start instead of a ~1ms `/bin/sh` fork on every bounded disposable command.
- The two shapes it could take are both worse than they look: the exported-verb form (mirroring `trust.RunVerifierChild`) is a **breaking consumer contract** that fork-bombs every out-of-tree consumer's suite until it adds the intercept; the `init()`-intercept form is genuinely fork-bomb-safe by construction but buries an env-triggered arbitrary-exec primitive in every consumer binary's `init()`.

## The decision

Delete `trap ':' TERM` and its paired `trap - TERM` restore (the restore only exists to undo the mask, and exec'd programs inherit SIG_IGN dispositions anyway). Keep the ready marker and the gate read. One red-provable test: SIGTERM kills a child parked at the gate. One honestly-labelled regression guard: EOF → 125, bounded in time and CPU.

## Acceptance criterion amended

"**No `trap` anywhere in the tree**" is WITHDRAWN as unachievable and harmful. Every other `trap` in the tree is a deliberate TERM-ignoring **test subject** proving SIGKILL escalation works: `proc/manager_test.go:690`, `proc/reaper_test.go:1794` (`startTermIgnorer`, which the child-record-lifetime contract itself pins at its line 70 as the proof for the five-times-widened identity tuple), `worker/pool_test.go:317,410,571,674`, `service/runner_test.go:39`, `daemon/child_fence_test.go:62`, `daemon/runtime_rewrite_test.go:723,750,800`, `trust/process_verifier_test.go:78`, plus two ordinary `trap … EXIT` cleanups in `scripts/`. Deleting them would delete the escalation ladder's own proofs.

The replacement criterion is **"no `trap` in non-test Go source"** — a one-site check.
